artifacts.summary: 4-phase, 4.5-hour plan for a bare-registered blocking PreToolUse Bash hook enforcing bounded-build-waiter.md Rule 2, with fixture suite, manifest wiring, and deploy-time live-fire proof.

memory_candidates.content: A PreToolUse hook that must FAIL OPEN cannot use bare jq calls under `set -euo pipefail`. jq exits 2 on usage/system errors; a set -e abort propagates the failing command's exit code; and exit 2 is precisely the code PreToolUse reads as BLOCK. So an unguarded jq failure inverts fail-open into fail-closed and blocks every matching tool call repo-wide. The established fix in this codebase is to append `|| true` to every jq invocation plus a `command -v jq` gate ahead of first use (see hooks/validate-no-task-references.sh). The general pattern: in any hook whose fail-open contract is expressed through exit codes, audit every helper binary whose own error exit code collides with the framework's blocking code -- the collision, not the failure itself, is the defect.
